claims.text: The initial CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy is single phase.
The initial alloy has a uniform distribution of constituent elements.
The initial alloy has a homogeneous grain structure.
Applied stress under particular temperature and strain-rate conditions induces dynamic nanoclustering at grain boundaries in CoCrFeMnNi.
Cr, Mn, and Ni are among the principal elements that dynamically segregate at grain boundaries.
Stress-driven grain-boundary segregation reduces local grain-boundary cohesion.
Reduced grain-boundary cohesion promotes early intergranular crack initiation.
Intergranular crack initiation caused by dynamic segregation produces a transition from ductile to brittle failure.
Applied stress increases atomic mobility at grain boundaries.
Increased grain-boundary atomic mobility enables rapid, non-equilibrium elemental segregation.
Intermediate strain rates provide a balance between diffusion kinetics and imposed mechanical loading that favors segregation-assisted cracking.
At moderate temperatures and intermediate strain rates, grain boundaries will exhibit more elemental segregation than the low-strain-rate or unloaded baseline.
Regions with enhanced grain-boundary segregation will correlate with intergranular crack initiation and brittle fracture features.
Lower strain rates reduce atomic mobility and stress-driven segregation relative to intermediate strain rates.
Low-strain-rate specimens will retain more uniform grain-boundary compositions and ductile fracture behavior.
The proposed mechanism can operate at service-relevant temperatures up to approximately 250 °C.
Loading conditions that freeze atomic mobility or cause substantial adiabatic heating fall outside the proposed mechanism's operating regime.
